title: Forced unwraps can turn expected assertion failures into test crashes
reasoning: Swift Testing `#expect` records an expectation failure but does not provide a safely unwrapped value for subsequent assertions. If `errorDescription` regresses to nil, these tests immediately force-unwrap `desc!`, producing a runtime trap instead of a clean assertion that pinpoints the missing localized description. The same pattern is repeated across all description tests.
reproduction: Change any tested `errorDescription` branch to return nil, then run the AWSConfigINITests target; the test will hit the forced unwrap after the nil expectation rather than using a structured require failure.
recommendation: Make the description tests throwing and unwrap with `try #require(error.errorDescription)` before checking contents. This preserves the intended nil check while avoiding fatal unwraps.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The issue is in the test implementation itself: the nil assertion is followed by an unsafe unwrap in the same test, so there is no separate coverage for the failure mode.
minimumFixScope: Update each `let desc = error.errorDescription; #expect(desc != nil); #expect(desc!.contains(...))` sequence in `AWSConfigINIErrorTests` to `let desc = try #require(error.errorDescription)` and mark those test methods as throwing.
